subject: anatomy
title: Female reproductive organs: uterus, supports, ovary, tube, vagina and lymphatics

steps.tx: The **uterus** is a pear-shaped muscular organ lying between the bladder in front and the rectum behind. Its cervix protrudes into the vagina. The uterus is normally anteverted, meaning tilted forward, and anteflexed, meaning the body bends forward on the cervix. Examiners often ask about the position of the uterus, so learn these two terms together.

vis.alt: Table diagram of the five ligaments of the uterus with their attachments and roles: cardinal ligament main support, uterosacral keeps anteversion, round ligament to labium majus, broad ligament peritoneal fold, pubocervical to pubis.
vis.caption: The cardinal ligament is the main support; the round ligament holds the uterus anteverted and runs through the inguinal canal.

steps.tx: The **broad ligament** has three parts: the mesometrium, mesosalpinx and mesovarium. The **ovary** lies in the ovarian fossa on the lateral pelvic wall, bounded in front by the obliterated umbilical artery and behind by the ureter and internal iliac artery. The suspensory or infundibulopelvic ligament carries the ovarian vessels, and the ovarian artery crosses the ureter at the pelvic brim.

steps.tx: The **uterine artery** is a branch of the anterior division of the **internal iliac artery**. It lies near the ureter, which runs below and lateral to the cervix, about 1 cm from the supravaginal cervix. The ureter is the structure most at risk during hysterectomy ligation. Lymph from the cervix drains to external iliac, internal iliac and sacral nodes, while the fundus drains mainly to para-aortic nodes.

steps.tx: The **fallopian tube** has four parts from lateral to medial: infundibulum, ampulla, isthmus and intramural part. The ampulla is the widest part and the usual site of fertilisation. The intramural part is the shortest and narrowest, so only a fine cannula passes during salpingostomy. The tube is lined by ciliated columnar epithelium with peg cells. Mullerian ducts form the tubes, uterus and vagina.

steps.tx: The **vagina** is a muscular tube lined by **stratified squamous epithelium** with no glands of its own. Its wall has no mucous glands, and secretions come from cervical mucus and transudation. The posterior wall is longer than the anterior. The **posterior fornix** is the largest recess and is the site for culdocentesis. Vaginal closure is aided by the pubovaginalis, bulbospongiosus and external urethral sphincter.
